purpose: ONE registered experiment, TWO paired arms, on this study's own Earnings-22 DEV subset10 cut at the ESB train-split boundaries: 6,038 utterances, one contact per utterance per arm. Arm A sends the instruction the sealed ESB TEST flight sent, byte for byte. Arm B sends the Qwen3-Omni authors' own English ASR prompt from the official model card and cookbook. Everything else is identical between the arms. The question is whether the prompt explains the ESB test flight's NOT ALIGNED 15.937 -- whose error shape was output discipline (insertions 59.2 % of errors, hypothesis 1.0749x the reference length, an oracle length cut worth 5.48 points) rather than recognition. Preregistration: docs/readiness/2026-09-05-e22-dev-esb-prompt-ab-v1-preregistration.md.

predecessor.result: NOT ALIGNED, corpus Whisper-normalized WER 15.937 over all 2,735 published ESB test utterances against a published same-model 9.79 and a cross-read 12.3
predecessor.what_it_supplies_here: the harness, the entry point, the audio path, the build, the decoding params, the scorers, the reference rail, the roster/reference/D1 receipt shapes, the smoke design and arm A's instruction -- everything except the population, the instruction under test and the slot size the longer utterances force

owner_directive_2026_09_05: Align the PROMPT and the model usage first. The confirmatory read of the six ESB test calls is spent; the prompt is chosen on the DEV split, and the owner then decides whether a second and final test read is made.

primary.source: NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel, 'Fine-Tune Qwen3-Omni for ASR'
primary.protocol: Whisper EnglishTextNormalizer both sides, greedy, N = 2741 utterances of the ESB Earnings22 TEST subset
primary.note: the ONLY same-model published number across this study's three carriers -- and it is computed over the TEST subset, NOT over these ten dev calls. It appears here as an INDICATION ONLY.

cross_read.system: Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct on the Open ASR Leaderboard English subset
cross_read.note: two vendor reports of the SAME frozen model that disagree by 2.5 points

paper_row.population_caveat: NO published number exists for these ten calls. Nothing in this experiment is an alignment verdict. The 3-point band around 9.79 / 12.3 is reported for orientation only and is explicitly labelled as such wherever it appears.

E22-ESB-DEV10-UTTERANCES.selection: no draw: every ESB train-split utterance of all ten registered dev calls
E22-ESB-DEV10-UTTERANCES.estimand: the paired within-utterance effect of the instruction on corpus WER, on a population this study is allowed to optimize on

cells.factor: the instruction: the one the sealed ESB test flight sent

cells.serving_geometry: -c 40960 -np 8, 5120 tokens per slot -- identical to arm A
cells.factor: the instruction: the Qwen3-Omni authors' own English ASR prompt

shared_protocol.audio_path: raw audio, bf16 mmproj resident on the GPU, no feature cache directory
shared_protocol.obs: none -- an ESB utterance IS the request; there is no windowing here
shared_protocol.harness: core.flight.FlightRuntime with the shared rails zero-supply direct arm and the OpenJiuwen executor, entered through scripts/flights/run_e22_esb_cell.py -- the same harness and entry point the sealed ESB test flight used
shared_protocol.prompt_shape: the base TaskAdapter.assemble_prompt default: one system message carrying the instruction, one user message carrying the audio. IDENTICAL in both arms.
shared_protocol.instruction_arm_a: Transcribe the speech verbatim exactly as spoken. Never insert, repeat, or add any word you do not clearly hear in the audio. Output only the transcript text.
shared_protocol.instruction_arm_b: Transcribe the English audio into text.
shared_protocol.the_only_difference: the task_instruction string, and nothing else. Same roster, same media bytes, same reference layer, same scorers, same build, same geometry, same decoding params, same harness, same entry point, same prompt shape.

deviations.deviation: serving geometry -c 40960 -np 8 (5120 tokens per slot) rather than the sealed ESB test flight's -c 32768 -np 8 (4096)
deviations.why: this roster's longest utterance is 78.360000 s against the test roster's 36.360125 s, so the worst request needs about 2102 tokens and 2 x 2102 = 4204 exceeds a 4096-token slot; the repository's own fit rule (slot_tokens >= 2 x worst_required) refuses the smaller geometry on this population
deviations.expected_effect: none on any transcript: the geometry changes no request byte, and it is identical in both arms so it cannot touch the paired contrast

deviations.deviation: arm B keeps the system-message prompt shape although the Qwen3-Omni model card says 'No system prompt should be set for any evaluation benchmark' and puts the prompt text in the user turn AFTER the audio
deviations.why: one factor at a time: this experiment measures the instruction TEXT, and changing the message placement at the same time would confound the two
deviations.expected_effect: unknown; message placement and the system role are named as a SECOND, UNFLOWN suspect and are reported to the owner rather than flown here

deviations.deviation: the population is the ten dev calls, not the published ESB test subset
deviations.why: the confirmatory read of the six ESB test calls is spent; dev is the split this study may optimize on
deviations.expected_effect: no number here is an alignment verdict, and the published 9.79 / 12.3 appear as an indication only

deviations.why: this study's Whisper-normalizer scorer does not implement it
deviations.expected_effect: identical in both arms, so it cancels in the contrast

evaluation.paper_facing_aggregation: corpus: total S+D+I over total reference words
metrics: corpus WER under the Whisper EnglishTextNormalizer, per arm, pooled and per call (paper-facing)
mean of per-utterance WER under the same normalizer
corpus and mean WER under the frozen saea-scoring-v1 normalizer
substitutions / deletions / insertions and reference words, per arm
hypothesis-to-reference length ratio and the insertion share of errors, per arm
the paired per-utterance contrast B minus A: saves / harms / ties, exact sign test, 10,000 call-stratified bootstrap replicates, seed 20260903, CI90

paired_analysis.metric_convention: the per-utterance metric passed to analysis.paired is NEGATED WER, so delta = right - left = A_wer - B_wer is POSITIVE when arm B is better and 'saves' counts utterances arm B improves. The raw B - A WER delta is reported beside it.

mandatory_slices: the per-call table for all ten dev calls, corpus WER under both normalizers, both arms
natural-mixture (corpus) and equal-call weightings side by side, both arms
the insertion / deletion / substitution split and the hypothesis-to-reference length ratio, both arms
the one utterance whose end boundary was clamped to the decoded parent, named
whether arm B's dev number would sit inside the 3-point band of 9.79 / 12.3, stated explicitly as an INDICATION ONLY because dev is not the test subset

execution_plan_basis.planned_model_calls: PER ARM: 6,038 rows x 1 contact + 8 canaries = 6,046; the registered exposure ceiling per arm is 6,350 (about 5 % above the pass). Two arms = two run ids = two rows; core/model/adapter.py meters each plan cumulatively across every attempt of ITS OWN run id.
execution_plan_basis.planned_speech_audio_seconds: PER ARM: 39,292.64675 s for one pass, rounded up to 39,300; the registered ceiling per arm is 41,300, about 5 % above the pass. Both arms together are 78,585 s = 21.83 h of audio.
execution_plan_basis.planned_gpu_hours: PER ARM 0.5, registered ceiling 0.75, i.e. 1.0 planned and 1.5 registered across the experiment. Basis: the sealed ESB test flight served 2,735 contacts over 19,494.6 s of audio in 0.226 GPU-h at -np 8 with graphs disabled (3.54 contacts/s, 25.2x realtime). This arm is 2.21x that in contacts and 2.02x in audio, so about 0.47 GPU-h is expected and 0.75 is 1.6x that.
execution_plan_basis.ceilings_live_in_the_exposure_row: contracts.ExecutionPlan carries no ceiling field; the registered ceilings are the exposure-ledger row's calls / speech audio seconds / gpu hours cells, which the gate requires to be at least these planned values.

decision.rule: The arm with the LOWER pooled corpus Whisper-normalized WER becomes this study's ASR instruction for cleaned-reference protocols.
decision.significance_rule: If the CI90 lower bound on the paired delta (negated-WER convention, so 'above 0' means arm B genuinely lower WER) is NOT above 0, then the prompt is NOT the explanation for the ESB test flight's gap, and the next suspect is NAMED for the owner without being flown: (a) context-free clipping -- one sentence-length clip with no context and no way to know where it ends, the deviation D1 the test verdict already implicated through a length ratio that rises monotonically as clips shorten; and (b) the prompt SHAPE rather than its text -- the official protocol sets no system prompt and puts the instruction after the audio, which this experiment holds fixed on purpose (deviation G2).
decision.band_indication_only: The verdict states whether arm B's dev corpus WER would sit inside the 3-point band of the published 9.79 (and of the cross-read 12.3) as an INDICATION ONLY. These ten calls are not the test subset, no published number covers them, and no alignment verdict is issued here.
decision.claim_surface: No superiority, generality or Stage-3 claim. No mechanism arm. This is a prompt selection on a dev split, nothing more.
decision.not_authorized: No read of any confirmatory call. No second read of the six calibration-exposed ESB test calls. No third prompt variant. No few-shot. No post-processing of any hypothesis. No Q8_0 cell. No message-placement arm. No test tuning, no paper-scale work.

companion_run.why_separate: contracts.gate_exposure requires exactly one pre-registered exposure row per run id whose split identity hash equals the plan's, and the smoke's four rows have a different split identity hash and a much smaller budget, so it cannot share a run id with either flight arm.
